what: Same-host cost of a new device receiving every record of a collection, before and after receiving in pages with one rebuild of the rows per page and a lazily rebuilt engine index
source_commit: 948900bd908ce8eb30471ca8a40a53dde783ecfc (branch core/batch-receive; the measured code is unchanged in what merges)
baseline: docs/evidence/sync-checkpoint-cost-2026-11-21.json, replay_every_record_ms: one record at a time, a full projection rebuild and an engine reindex per record

host.name: betelgeuse
host.sqlite: bundled, WAL, synchronous=FULL as the app opens it
host.conditions: shared development host with other sessions; no CPU pinning; one run per workload

workload: the checkpoint cost example's: n tasks with 1 KiB notes, a rename of every second and a completion of every tenth, each edit its own sealed record (1.6 n records), received by a new device in pages of 256 as the sync client hands them over
findings: Receiving every record is 13 to 69 times faster on these workloads.
Doubling the records now takes about 2.4 times as long, against about 4 times before: the remaining growth is one rebuild of the rows per page of 256.
pages_only_ms shows the rows rebuilt once per page but the index still rebuilt per record: the index was the larger share of the remaining cost.
limits: One host, one run per workload.
Relay transfer time is not included: the device reads local bytes.
One writer; the receive work per record also authenticates its ML-DSA-65 signature, which is linear.
source_note: crates/matters-core/examples/checkpoint_cost.rs; the receiving device is checked to hold the same tasks as the source.
